# Flow 5: retiring things from the tree.
#
# retro removes a resource from the tree. The integration that served it is a folder in the
# integrations directory, and it stays there: another resource can use it, and nothing about
# retiring a resource is an uninstall.

step set up: a project with a git resource
exec orbiter --output json vessel init -y
exec orbiter --output json galaxy add acme
exec orbiter --output json planet add api --galaxy acme
exec orbiter --output json resource add git --role tool --brand git
exec orbiter --output json attach git api
exec orbiter survey api
stdout 'tool/git'

step retire the resource: it leaves the tree
exec orbiter --output json retro git -y
stdout '"retired":true'
exec orbiter survey api
! stdout 'tool/git'

step the integration is untouched: its folder is still there, and another resource can use it
exists $HOME/.orbiter/integrations/git/manifest.toml
exists $HOME/.orbiter/integrations/git/git.wasm
exec orbiter --output json resource add git2 --role tool --brand git
exec orbiter --output json attach git2 api
exec orbiter survey api
stdout 'tool/git'

step retire the planet: it and what hangs from it leave the tree
exec orbiter --output json retro api -y
stdout '"retired":true'
! exec orbiter survey api
exists $HOME/.orbiter/integrations/git/manifest.toml

step retiring a galaxy retires what is under it, leaf first
exec orbiter galaxy add bigcorp
exec orbiter planet add billing --galaxy bigcorp
exec orbiter retro bigcorp --yes
stdout 'bigcorp'
stdout 'retire|retired'
! exec orbiter survey bigcorp
stderr 'not found|no target'
! exec orbiter survey billing
stderr 'not found|no target'
